pharm: Aminoglycoside antibiotic (neomycin B) for topical, eye, and ear use that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis against susceptible Gram-negative and Gram-positive organisms.
quick: Eye/ear drops 1-2 drops several times daily; skin: apply gauze/cream to affected area as directed
Use only if necessary; avoid prolonged use on large areas
Minimal systemic absorption from intact surfaces; caution on broken skin
Local reaction/sensitisation; ototoxicity if used on large raw areas or perforated eardrum
summary: Framycetin (framycetin sulfate, essentially neomycin B) is an aminoglycoside antibiotic used topically and as eye and ear preparations - including impregnated gauze dressings (e.g., Sofra-Tulle), eye/ear drops, and combination products - for superficial bacterial infections of the skin, eye, and ear. It is not FDA-approved (used in the UK/Europe/India/Australia per SmPC/BNF). Like other aminoglycosides it inhibits bacterial protein synthesis and is active against many Gram-negative bacilli and staphylococci but not most streptococci, anaerobes, or Pseudomonas reliably. Because of poor systemic absorption it acts locally; the main concerns are contact allergic sensitisation and, with use on large raw areas or in the ear with a perforated eardrum, potential ototoxicity from systemic absorption.
indications: Superficial bacterial skin infections, infected wounds, ulcers, and burns (topical, including medicated gauze dressings)
Bacterial conjunctivitis, blepharitis, and other superficial eye infections (eye drops/ointment)
Bacterial otitis externa (ear drops, often combined with a corticosteroid)
Prevention of infection in minor wounds and skin grafts/donor sites

dosage.d: Apply framycetin-impregnated gauze or cream to the affected area and cover; renew dressing daily or as directed
dosage.n: Limit to small areas and short courses; per SmPC

dosage.d: Instill 1-2 drops into the affected eye(s) several times daily (e.g., every 1-2 hours acutely, reducing as infection responds)
dosage.n: Reduce frequency as the infection improves

dosage.d: Instill 2-3 drops into the affected ear 2-4 times daily (often combined with a corticosteroid such as dexamethasone)
dosage.n: Do not use if the eardrum is perforated; limit course to about 7 days

dosage.d: Apply a small amount to the affected eye at night or as directed

admin: For the eye: wash hands, instill drops into the conjunctival sac, and avoid touching the dropper to the eye
For the ear: ensure the eardrum is intact before use; warm the bottle to body temperature and instill with the head tilted
For the skin: clean the area, apply the dressing/cream, and limit to small areas and short courses
Do not use on extensive raw/denuded skin (risk of systemic absorption and ototoxicity)
Stop and seek advice if local redness, itching, or swelling suggests contact allergy
moa: Framycetin (neomycin B) is an aminoglycoside that binds irreversibly to the 30S subunit of the bacterial ribosome. This impairs the proofreading of the genetic code, causing misreading of messenger RNA and production of nonfunctional proteins, and blocks the initiation and elongation of protein synthesis. The resulting defective protein synthesis is bactericidal. Its spectrum covers many aerobic Gram-negative bacilli and staphylococci; it is unreliable against streptococci, anaerobes, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to framycetin, neomycin, or other aminoglycosides
Perforated tympanic membrane (for ear drops - risk of ototoxicity)
Use on extensively damaged skin or large raw areas (systemic absorption/ototoxicity)
relative: Use in the eye when a viral, fungal, or mycobacterial cause is possible (with steroid combinations)
monitor: Local allergic/contact reactions with prolonged use
Hearing if used on large denuded areas or with a perforated eardrum
Resolution of infection / emergence of resistant organisms or superinfection

preg: Topical/local framycetin has minimal systemic absorption from intact surfaces. Use during pregnancy only if necessary, and avoid prolonged application to large or broken-skin areas where systemic absorption (and theoretical fetal ototoxicity) could occur.
lact: Topical and local ophthalmic/otic use results in negligible systemic exposure and is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding. Avoid applying directly to the breast area before nursing.
renal: Systemic absorption from intact skin, the eye, or an intact ear is minimal, so no renal adjustment is needed for normal topical use. However, application to large raw areas can cause systemic absorption with the usual aminoglycoside risks (nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity) - avoid in renal impairment in that setting.
hepatic: No hepatic dose adjustment is required for topical/local use.

major: Systemic aminoglycosides or other ototoxic/nephrotoxic drugs - additive ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity if framycetin is significantly absorbed (e.g., from large raw areas or perforated eardrum)
moderate: Potent diuretics (e.g., furosemide) - increase aminoglycoside ototoxicity if absorbed
Neuromuscular blocking agents - aminoglycosides can potentiate blockade if absorbed systemically
minor: Other topical agents at the same site may increase irritation/sensitisation
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic systemic laboratory interference with topical use; patch testing may confirm contact allergy.

serious: Ototoxicity (with absorption from large raw areas or perforated eardrum)
Superinfection with resistant organisms or fungi
emergency: Significant hearing loss from systemic absorption

monitoring: Local skin/eye/ear for allergic or irritant reactions
Hearing if applied to large raw areas or used with a perforated eardrum
Therapeutic response and emergence of resistant organisms/superinfection
counsel: Use only on the affected area for the short course your doctor prescribes
For ear drops, do not use if you have a hole in your eardrum; tell your doctor if you have ear surgery or hearing problems
Stop and tell your doctor if the treated skin, eye, or ear becomes more red, itchy, or swollen (possible allergy)
Do not share drops or dressings, and discard eye/ear drops after the recommended period once opened
Avoid applying to large open wounds or burns unless specifically directed
pk: Local antibacterial action begins on contact with the infected site
Minimal systemic absorption from intact skin, eye, or intact ear
Not clinically relevant for topical use (poorly absorbed; the absorbed fraction is renally excreted unchanged)
Store at controlled room temperature; protect drops from contamination and discard after the stated in-use period
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - used in the UK/Europe/India/Australia (SmPC/BNF data); framycetin sulfate is essentially neomycin B
Common cause of CONTACT ALLERGIC dermatitis (cross-reacts with neomycin) - suspect if a treated rash worsens
Do NOT use ear drops with a perforated eardrum - absorbed aminoglycoside is ototoxic
Avoid on large raw/burned areas - systemic absorption can cause oto-/nephrotoxicity
Poor activity against Pseudomonas, streptococci, and anaerobes - choose another agent for these
missed: If you miss an application or instillation, apply it when you remember. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not apply a double amount.
overdose: Topical overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity from intact skin. Excessive application to large raw areas or instillation into a perforated ear could allow enough absorption to risk aminoglycoside ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Management is to discontinue use, irrigate/remove excess where applicable, and provide supportive care with monitoring of hearing and renal function if significant absorption is suspected.
